note: Contrast inventory for D3 only. Built to the same shape as the ERC-4337 inventory but deliberately small: the point is to measure how much the applicable set varies across contracts in a mature, homogeneous domain, not to audit ERC-20 tokens. One annotator is sufficient because this is a baseline, and that is stated in the paper.

obligations.statement: transfer and transferFrom must return a boolean and callers must check it
obligations.source_class: ERC-20 spec; the USDT non-returning class

obligations.statement: approve must be guarded against the allowance race, or a safe increase/decrease path provided
obligations.source_class: ERC-20 spec note; long-standing audit class

obligations.statement: transferFrom must not silently succeed when the allowance is insufficient
transfer of zero value must not revert
the contract must not assume the amount received equals the amount sent (fee-on-transfer)
balance must not be assumed constant between reads (rebasing)
decimals must be honoured by any arithmetic on amounts
totalSupply must equal the sum of balances across every mint, burn and transfer path
burn must not allow burning another holder's balance without allowance
a pause or blacklist mechanism must not permanently strand funds
permit must follow EIP-2612: domain separator with chainId and address(this), a nonce, and a deadline
permit must be resistant to signature malleability and must reject the zero address recovery
hooks or callbacks in transfer must not enable reentrancy into the token or its integrators
an upgradeable token must preserve storage layout and must not leave the implementation initialisable
